# Research program (generation 0)

## Goal
Find a policy-network architecture that raises dev success at a fixed training budget. Only the network changes; the training recipe, observation, reward and budget are fixed.

## How to run each round
1. Read every result so far, including failures. A difference of a few points between two trials can be seed noise; compare against the noise figure given in the task.
2. Write down what the evidence suggests before proposing anything.
3. Propose a mix:
   - about half the candidates refine the current best architecture with one main change each, so that each result says something clear;
   - the rest test a new idea that the results so far have not covered.
4. Give every candidate a hypothesis: what changes, why it should help on this task, and what result would refute it.
5. Think about the structure of the task when choosing ideas, not only generic network tricks: what the agent must perceive and decide to place the right brick in the right order.
6. Keep each file simple and correct. A candidate that fails the checks wastes a trial. Stay well inside the parameter and compute caps, because a slower network risks the time limit.
7. Do not repeat an idea that clearly failed unless you can say what is different this time.

## Revising this program
After each generation of searches, this program is rewritten by you from the logs of those searches, and then used for new searches, including on worlds of other sizes that you will not see while revising it. When revising:
- keep advice that the evidence supports, and say what evidence supports it;
- remove or weaken advice that did not help;
- write lessons that should hold on other grid sizes, not facts that only fit one world;
- keep the whole program under 1,000 words, including this section, which you may also improve.


## How the program is used
At the start of every round of every architecture search you receive this program together with a fixed task description, the interface rules, the starting architecture, the search's results so far (every trial's code, hypothesis and scores) and the budget. Each search has 2 rounds of 2 candidates and starts from the same starting architecture. The program is the only part of the procedure you can change. Next it will be used for new searches, including on brick worlds of other sizes that you will not see while revising it. It will be judged by how well the architectures found under it do on hidden designs, at the same budget.

## The fixed task description, as given in this generation's searches
## Task
An agent must build a target design in a brick world.
- The world is a 6 x 6 base, up to 4 layers high. Bricks are one layer high with footprints 1x1, 1x2, 2x1 or 2x2.
- A placed brick drops until it rests on the highest filled cell under its footprint (or the ground), so overhangs with empty cells under them are possible and placement order matters.
- Each step the agent picks a brick type and an anchor cell, or DONE. An episode ends at DONE or after 25 placements. Bricks cannot be removed.
- Target designs are made by 4 to 12 random brick drops. Training uses a stream of fresh random designs; the held-out designs never appear in training.

## Training and evaluation (fixed: you change only the network)
- Compute-matched budget: each trial trains a PPO agent from scratch on one CPU core with the same training compute as the starting architecture gets in 8,192 environment steps. A network whose training FLOPs per sample are r times the starting architecture's trains for 8,192 / r steps (rounded down to whole updates of 1,024 steps); a cheaper network still gets 8,192 steps. So a bigger network sees fewer designs. The recipe is fixed: Adam with learning rate 0.001 decaying linearly to 0, 64 parallel worlds, 16-step rollouts, 4 PPO epochs of 8 minibatches, gamma 0.95, GAE lambda 0.9, clip 0.2, entropy coefficient 0.01, value coefficient 0.5, gradient-norm clip 1.0, normalised advantages. Reward per placement: (target cells filled minus cells filled outside the target) / the target's cell count, minus 0.01; plus 1 when the episode ends with an exact build.
- A trial that runs longer than 600 seconds is killed and counts as a failure. Bigger or slower networks take longer.
- After training, the agent runs greedily on 512 held-out dev designs. Success means the finished build equals the target design exactly, cell for cell.
- Selection metric: dev success (higher is better). At the end of the search, the trial with the highest dev success is selected. It is then retrained with new seeds and tested once on a separate hidden set of designs, so a lucky seed does not help.
- Noise: every trial trains 1 seed and reports the mean dev success. The starting architecture, trained with 2 different seeds, scored 0.000, 0.000 on dev (mean 0.000): training runs on this task can succeed or fail by seed luck alone, so treat single differences of this size with care.

Your analysis before round 1: There is no trial evidence yet. The 2D conv baseline scored 0.000 on both seeds. The budget is tiny (8,192 steps), so the network needs strong inductive biases. A good placement depends on two things. First, the brick's landing layer, which is the max of the build heights under its footprint. Second, whether the target fills the footprint at that layer without leaving missing cells beneath it, so nothing gets sealed off. The baseline's 1x1 head sees only the anchor cell and has to infer both of these, which is hard in so few updates. Both candidates therefore build a feature vector for each brick type and anchor. They pool over the brick's footprint and add fixed, footprint-pooled landing-layer features: a one-hot of the landing layer, target fill at that layer and the one above, missing cells that would be buried, and height gaps. Learned 1x1 layers then score them. The candidates differ in their trunk: a plain 2D conv trunk versus a per-layer (3D-aware) trunk whose features are read at the landing layer. Both stay under the baseline's FLOPs, so each gets the full 8,192 steps.
Your analysis before round 2: All three architectures score 0. That includes r1 and r2, which already compute footprint landing features, so having the right features is not enough by itself. The budget is very small: 8 PPO updates, about 256 Adam steps. In r1 and r2 the hand features pass through a small-init MLP. A logit can then move only about 0.1 to 0.3 during training, which is too little to change greedy argmax choices over roughly 145 actions. DONE is a second weak point. Success needs DONE chosen exactly when nothing is missing or extra, but the DONE head only sees mean-pooled channels, and complete builds are rare in random play. Plan: add a zero-initialised linear path with an input gain, from per-action landing features straight to the logits, so learning moves the logits faster. Give the DONE and value heads explicit global features: fraction missing, fraction extra, an exact-build indicator and time. The two candidates differ in gain (8 vs 3) and in whether reward-like cell-count features are included. Caveat: the 2% post-training check may cap how high any trial can score.

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 48
HID = 32


def fp_pool(x, dy, dx, mode):
    if dy > 1 or dx > 1:
        x = F.pad(x, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
    if mode == 'max':
        return F.max_pool2d(x, (dy, dx), stride=1)
    return F.avg_pool2d(x, (dy, dx), stride=1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        Z = spec.Z
        self.Z = Z
        self.T = spec.n_types
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for (a, b) in spec.footprints]
        C = spec.in_channels
        self.body = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(C, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        nin = WIDTH + (Z + 6) + self.T
        self.head1 = nn.Conv2d(nin, HID, 1)
        self.head2 = nn.Conv2d(HID, 1, 1)
        nn.init.uniform_(self.head2.weight, -0.01, 0.01)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.head2.bias)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH + C, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def hand(self, obs, dy, dx):
        Z = self.Z
        hb = torch.round(obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 1] * Z)
        ht = torch.round(obs[:, 4 * Z + 1:4 * Z + 2] * Z)
        L = fp_pool(hb, dy, dx, 'max')
        zs1 = torch.arange(Z + 1, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, -1, 1, 1)
        oh = (L == zs1).to(obs.dtype)
        tavg = fp_pool(obs[:, Z:2 * Z], dy, dx, 'avg')
        mavg = fp_pool(obs[:, 2 * Z:3 * Z], dy, dx, 'avg')
        tL = (oh[:, :Z] * tavg).sum(1, keepdim=True)
        tA = (oh[:, :Z - 1] * tavg[:, 1:]).sum(1, keepdim=True)
        below = (L > zs1[:, :Z]).to(obs.dtype)
        gm = (below * mavg).sum(1, keepdim=True)
        flat = (L - fp_pool(hb, dy, dx, 'avg')) / Z
        tg = (fp_pool(ht, dy, dx, 'avg') - L) / Z
        return torch.cat([oh, tL, tA, gm, flat, tg], 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, _, Y, X = obs.shape
        f = self.body(obs)
        feats = []
        for t, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.fps):
            ft = fp_pool(f, dy, dx, 'avg')
            h = self.hand(obs, dy, dx)
            to = obs.new_zeros(B, self.T, Y, X)
            to[:, t] = 1.0
            feats.append(torch.cat([ft, h, to], 1))
        x = torch.cat(feats, 0)
        p = self.head2(F.relu(self.head1(x)))
        place = p.reshape(self.T, B, Y * X).permute(1, 0, 2).reshape(B, -1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3)), obs.mean((2, 3))], 1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], 1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)
```

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WC = 24
HID = 32


def fp_pool(x, dy, dx, mode):
    if dy > 1 or dx > 1:
        x = F.pad(x, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
    if mode == 'max':
        return F.max_pool2d(x, (dy, dx), stride=1)
    return F.avg_pool2d(x, (dy, dx), stride=1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        Z = spec.Z
        self.Z = Z
        self.T = spec.n_types
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for (a, b) in spec.footprints]
        C = spec.in_channels
        self.layer_body = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(11, WC, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(WC, WC, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        nin = WC + (Z + 6) + self.T
        self.head1 = nn.Conv2d(nin, HID, 1)
        self.head2 = nn.Conv2d(HID, 1, 1)
        nn.init.uniform_(self.head2.weight, -0.01, 0.01)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.head2.bias)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WC + C, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def hand(self, obs, dy, dx):
        Z = self.Z
        hb = torch.round(obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 1] * Z)
        ht = torch.round(obs[:, 4 * Z + 1:4 * Z + 2] * Z)
        L = fp_pool(hb, dy, dx, 'max')
        zs1 = torch.arange(Z + 1, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, -1, 1, 1)
        oh = (L == zs1).to(obs.dtype)
        tavg = fp_pool(obs[:, Z:2 * Z], dy, dx, 'avg')
        mavg = fp_pool(obs[:, 2 * Z:3 * Z], dy, dx, 'avg')
        tL = (oh[:, :Z] * tavg).sum(1, keepdim=True)
        tA = (oh[:, :Z - 1] * tavg[:, 1:]).sum(1, keepdim=True)
        below = (L > zs1[:, :Z]).to(obs.dtype)
        gm = (below * mavg).sum(1, keepdim=True)
        flat = (L - fp_pool(hb, dy, dx, 'avg')) / Z
        tg = (fp_pool(ht, dy, dx, 'avg') - L) / Z
        return torch.cat([oh, tL, tA, gm, flat, tg], 1), oh

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, _, Y, X = obs.shape
        Z = self.Z
        b = obs[:, :Z]
        tg = obs[:, Z:2 * Z]
        ms = obs[:, 2 * Z:3 * Z]
        ex = obs[:, 3 * Z:4 * Z]
        one = obs.new_ones(B, 1, Y, X)
        zero = obs.new_zeros(B, 1, Y, X)
        bb = torch.cat([one, b[:, :Z - 1]], 1)
        tb = torch.cat([one, tg[:, :Z - 1]], 1)
        ta = torch.cat([tg[:, 1:], zero], 1)
        hbz = obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 1].expand(B, Z, Y, X)
        htz = obs[:, 4 * Z + 1:4 * Z + 2].expand(B, Z, Y, X)
        tm = obs[:, 4 * Z + 2:4 * Z + 3].expand(B, Z, Y, X)
        zc = (torch.arange(Z, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype) / Z).view(1, Z, 1, 1).expand(B, Z, Y, X)
        per = torch.stack([b, tg, ms, ex, bb, tb, ta, hbz, htz, zc, tm], 2)
        Fl = self.layer_body(per.reshape(B * Z, 11, Y, X))
        feats = []
        for t, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.fps):
            P = fp_pool(Fl, dy, dx, 'avg').reshape(B, Z, WC, Y, X)
            h, oh = self.hand(obs, dy, dx)
            sel = (oh[:, :Z].unsqueeze(2) * P).sum(1)
            to = obs.new_zeros(B, self.T, Y, X)
            to[:, t] = 1.0
            feats.append(torch.cat([sel, h, to], 1))
        x = torch.cat(feats, 0)
        p = self.head2(F.relu(self.head1(x)))
        place = p.reshape(self.T, B, Y * X).permute(1, 0, 2).reshape(B, -1)
        Fv = Fl.reshape(B, Z, WC, Y, X)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([Fv.mean((1, 3, 4)), Fv.amax((1, 3, 4)), obs.mean((2, 3))], 1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], 1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)
```

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 32
HID = 32
GAIN = 8.0
USE_COUNTS = True


def fp_pool(x, dy, dx, mode):
    if dy > 1 or dx > 1:
        x = F.pad(x, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
    if mode == 'max':
        return F.max_pool2d(x, (dy, dx), stride=1)
    return F.avg_pool2d(x, (dy, dx), stride=1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        Z = spec.Z
        self.Z = Z
        self.T = spec.n_types
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for (a, b) in spec.footprints]
        C = spec.in_channels
        self.body = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(C, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        nf = 11 if USE_COUNTS else 9
        self.lin = nn.Conv2d(nf + self.T, 1, 1)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.lin.weight)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.lin.bias)
        self.head1 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH + nf + self.T, HID, 1)
        self.head2 = nn.Conv2d(HID, 1, 1)
        nn.init.uniform_(self.head2.weight, -0.01, 0.01)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.head2.bias)
        NG = 6
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH + NG, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.done_lin = nn.Linear(NG, 1)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.done_lin.weight)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.done_lin.bias)
        self.value_lin = nn.Linear(NG, 1)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.value_lin.weight)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.value_lin.bias)

    def feats(self, obs, dy, dx, ntar):
        Z = self.Z
        hb = torch.round(obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 1] * Z)
        L = fp_pool(hb, dy, dx, 'max')
        zs = torch.arange(Z, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, -1, 1, 1)
        oh = (L == zs).to(obs.dtype)
        tavg = fp_pool(obs[:, Z:2 * Z], dy, dx, 'avg')
        mavg = fp_pool(obs[:, 2 * Z:3 * Z], dy, dx, 'avg')
        good = (oh * tavg).sum(1, keepdim=True)
        valid = (L < Z).to(obs.dtype)
        bad = (1.0 - good) * valid
        tA = (oh[:, :Z - 1] * tavg[:, 1:]).sum(1, keepdim=True)
        below = (L > zs).to(obs.dtype)
        gm = (below * mavg).sum(1, keepdim=True)
        bury = (gm > 1e-6).to(obs.dtype)
        full = (good > 0.999).to(obs.dtype)
        flat = (L - fp_pool(hb, dy, dx, 'avg')) / Z
        area = torch.ones_like(L) * (dy * dx / 4.0)
        fl = [good, bad, gm, bury, full, tA, flat, L / Z, area]
        if USE_COUNTS:
            fl = fl + [good * (dy * dx) / ntar, bad * (dy * dx) / ntar]
        return torch.cat(fl, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, _, Y, X = obs.shape
        Z = self.Z
        f = self.body(obs)
        tar = obs[:, Z:2 * Z].sum((1, 2, 3)).clamp(min=1.0)
        ntar = tar.view(B, 1, 1, 1)
        fts, hs, tos = [], [], []
        for t, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.fps):
            fts.append(fp_pool(f, dy, dx, 'avg'))
            hs.append(self.feats(obs, dy, dx, ntar))
            to = torch.zeros(B, self.T, Y, X, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype)
            to[:, t] = 1.0
            tos.append(to)
        ft = torch.cat(fts, 0)
        h = torch.cat(hs, 0)
        to = torch.cat(tos, 0)
        hl = torch.cat([h, to], 1)
        p = self.lin(hl * GAIN) + self.head2(F.relu(self.head1(torch.cat([ft, hl], 1))))
        place = p.reshape(self.T, B, Y * X).permute(1, 0, 2).reshape(B, -1)
        miss = obs[:, 2 * Z:3 * Z].sum((1, 2, 3))
        ext = obs[:, 3 * Z:4 * Z].sum((1, 2, 3))
        gf = torch.stack([miss / tar, (miss > 0.5).to(obs.dtype), ext / tar,
                          (ext > 0.5).to(obs.dtype), obs[:, 4 * Z + 2].mean((1, 2)),
                          ((miss + ext) < 0.5).to(obs.dtype)], 1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3)), gf], 1))
        done = self.done_head(g) + self.done_lin(gf * GAIN)
        value = self.value_head(g) + self.value_lin(gf)
        logits = torch.cat([place, done], 1)
        return logits, value.squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)
```

reply.lessons: All four trials in generation 0 scored 0.000 on dev, and all had 0.000 training success. They included the conv baseline, footprint landing-feature heads, a per-layer trunk read at the landing layer, and zero-initialised fast linear paths with gain 3 or 8. So computing the correct features is not enough. With about 8 PPO updates (around 256 Adam steps), a policy that starts near uniform over roughly 145 actions almost never completes an exact build. Without completed builds there is no success signal, so the policy cannot learn one. Adding gain to zero-initialised weights did not fix this, because those weights still start at zero. Making the network cheaper also gives no extra steps, since steps are capped at 8,192. The likely way out is an architecture that is already competent before training. Its learnable weights would start with a strong, structured prior: place bricks only where the whole footprint lands on target cells at the correct layer, bury nothing, build bottom-up, and choose DONE exactly when nothing is missing. Training then only fine-tunes this behaviour. On the search side, refining a best result of 0 taught nothing. Find a policy-network architecture that raises dev success at a fixed training budget. Only the network changes; the training recipe, observation, reward and budget are fixed.

## Core lesson so far (evidence: generation 0)
With a budget of about 8 PPO updates (roughly 256 Adam steps), a network that starts near uniform never completes an exact build. Without completed builds it gets no success signal, so it cannot learn one. Generation 0 tested four designs: the conv baseline, footprint landing features fed to a small-init MLP, a per-layer trunk read at the landing layer, and zero-initialised linear paths with gain 3 or 8. All scored 0.000 on dev and 0.000 on training success. Correct features are necessary but not enough. **The network must already be competent before training**, and training should only fine-tune it. Logits move only about 0.1–0.3 during training. That works in both directions: a well-set prior survives training, but a prior the network has to learn cannot form in time.

## How to build a competent prior
Compute exact per-action features with fixed operations that work at any grid size and height Z: pooling over the footprint for each brick type, and comparisons against the height maps. Then give the logits **non-zero, hand-set initial weights** on those features, with margins of several logits, plus a small learnable residual. Optionally keep part of the score as a fixed buffer so that the entropy bonus and noisy advantages cannot erase it. Useful terms:
- Landing layer L = max of the build heights under the footprint. Placing at L >= Z is invalid or bad.
- Good placement: every footprint cell is a target cell at layer L and currently missing. Give it a strong bonus.
- Any footprint cell that is not a target cell at L counts as extra cells, which can never be removed and so make an exact build impossible. Give it a strong penalty.
- Burying: a missing target cell below L under the footprint is sealed forever. Give it a strong penalty.
- Order: prefer the lowest landing layer first, so that supports exist before the layers above them.
- Overhangs (target cells with empty cells beneath them) can only be made by a multi-cell brick that rests on a filled cell elsewhere in its footprint. Prefer larger good bricks, and add a tie-break that favours footprints covering unsupported target cells.
- DONE: a strong positive logit exactly when missing = 0 and extra = 0, and strongly negative while good placements remain.
- Value head: give it the global features fraction missing, fraction extra, an exact-build flag and time.
Try to sanity-check the prior by reasoning: on a simple design, would greedy argmax build the target exactly? Look for features that are off by one (layer indexing, anchor/footprint alignment, padding at the edges).

Read the interface rules for any check on learnability, parameter use or how training changes the network, and obey them. If hand-set weights are disallowed or penalised, use an informed initialisation of learnable weights instead.

## How to run each round
1. Read every result so far, including failures and training success over the last 10%. Single-seed differences of a few points can be noise; compare against the task's noise figure.
2. Write down what the evidence suggests before proposing anything.
3. Propose a mix:
   - **While the best dev success is 0:** every candidate is a distinct, bold attempt at a nonzero score. Examples: different prior strengths, different tie-break and ordering rules, a fixed prior plus a learnable residual versus a fully learnable informed initialisation. Refining a 0-scoring design teaches nothing.
   - **Once something scores above 0:** about half the candidates refine the best one with one main change each; the rest test an idea the results have not covered.
4. Give every candidate a hypothesis: what changes, why it should help on this task, and what result would refute it.
5. Reason from the task's structure (what the agent must perceive and decide to place the right brick in the right order) rather than reaching for generic tricks such as more width or depth.
6. Keep files simple and correct. A candidate that fails the checks wastes a trial. Stay well inside the parameter and compute caps. A cheaper network gets **no** extra steps (steps are capped at the baseline's), so the only reason to keep a network small is speed and time-limit safety. Small, mostly fixed-feature networks are fine.
7. Do not repeat an idea that clearly failed unless you can say what is different. Already failed: learning from scratch on correct features, whether through a small-init MLP, a per-layer trunk, or a zero-initialised high-gain linear path.
8. Diagnostics: if training success is above 0 but dev is 0, suspect DONE timing or overfitting to training. If both are 0, the prior is not competent: check the feature definitions and margins.

## Revising this program
After each generation of searches, this program is rewritten by you from the logs of those searches, and then used for new searches, including on worlds of other sizes that you will not see while revising it. When revising:
- keep advice that the evidence supports, and say what evidence supports it;
- remove or weaken advice that did not help, including the competent-prior principle if trials built that way also score 0, and record why;
- write lessons that should hold on other grid sizes and heights: feature definitions must be size-agnostic (no hard-coded Y, X, Z or design counts);
- keep the whole program under 1,000 words, including this section, which you may also improve.
reply.expected_effect: Searches should produce architectures whose greedy policy builds some held-out designs exactly from the start and keeps that ability through the short training run. You can tell it worked if dev success and training success in the last 10% rise above 0 in at least one trial per search, ideally well above the baseline's 0.000 on both seeds, and if the selected architecture is no longer the starting one.
